sourceInstances.name: Factory tools
sourceInstances.ingestionGoal: Track the toolchain behind an agentic SDLC factory: the ACP TypeScript SDK, the Agent Host Protocol, Pierre, t3code, Effect, OpenCode, and the Pi SDK. Use only the configured sources. From base repositories and SDK documentation, extract durable general concepts, architecture, protocol and SDK capabilities, terminology, relationships, and usage guidance. From release pages, extract versioned release information, including release dates, breaking changes, compatibility changes, deprecations, fixes, and significant additions. For Effect, focus on the durable execution surface — Workflow, Activity, DurableQueue, and everything surrounding workflow definition, execution, persistence, and recovery — rather than the full API surface. Prefer cross-linking how these tools compose into one factory pipeline over isolated per-tool summaries. Preserve the canonical source URLs, update existing canonical concepts and references instead of creating duplicates, and exclude unrelated search results.

sourceInstances.name: Agent integration protocols
sourceInstances.ingestionGoal: Use only the configured agent integration protocol sources, currently the Model Context Protocol blog, the specification repository's release pages, and the MCP apps extension repository. Extract durable general concepts, architecture, protocol surfaces, terminology, relationships, and usage guidance for how agents integrate with external tools, data, and other agents: transports and session lifecycle, capability negotiation, the tool, resource, and prompt primitives, sampling and elicitation, authorization, server and client responsibilities, registries and extensions, including the apps extension's interface surface. From release and specification revision pages, extract versioned protocol information, including revision dates, breaking changes, compatibility changes, deprecations, fixes, and significant additions. Treat blog posts as announcements pointing at the specification rather than as durable pages of their own, and cross-link this protocol with the other protocols already in the wiki, including the generative UI efforts the apps extension relates to. Preserve the canonical source URLs, update existing canonical concepts and references instead of creating duplicates, and exclude unrelated search results.
